releases.notes:
# DarkMusic v3.5.1

## Improvements

- Audio profiles now offer Original, a blank Custom starting point, and saved profiles. Edited values belong to the selected profile, with Save updating the saved entry.
- Sound environments put Off in the picker, offer a blank Custom starting point, and keep saved environments selected while editing them.
- Selecting a song from a list preserves your Up Next queue.
- Settings ownership and the connections between screens, playback, HUD, PiP and background workers have been simplified.

## Fixes

- Retry Discord status connections every five seconds when Discord is opened after Minecraft.
- Prevent lost updates when library source evidence changes concurrently.
- Preserve the latest lyrics retry deadline when multiple workers update it.

## Compatibility

Install **`darkmusic-3.5.1.jar`** with **Minecraft 26.2**, **Java 25**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.5+** and **Fabric API for 26.2**. Existing libraries, playlists and settings remain supported. PiP and Media Controls remain optional Windows x64 extensions installed through their in-game menus; use the matching v3.5.1 packages. **Do not put extension ZIPs in `mods`**. The music player supports Windows, Linux and macOS.

releases.notes:
# DarkMusic v3.5.0

## New

- **Pick up where you left off.** DarkMusic remembers the last song, the collection it played from, and where it was. The player opens on it, and Play, the Play/Pause shortcut, `/da play` and Autoplay on Launch continue from there (**Settings → General → Resume Where You Left Off**, on by default).
- **Discord status (opt-in).** Show "Listening to DarkMusic" on your Discord profile with the song, artist and a progress bar. It talks to the Discord desktop app on your computer; nothing signs in. Songs downloaded from YouTube show the video's thumbnail. You can hide the song title (**Settings → General → Discord Status**).
- **Media keys and Windows media controls (optional, Windows x64).** After **Settings → General → Install Media Controls** (about 6 MB), keyboard media keys, headset buttons and the Windows media flyout control DarkMusic, and the flyout shows the song, artwork and timeline. Like PiP, it is installed only on request, checked against a fingerprint in the mod, kept outside `mods`, and runs as a separate program only while switched on. **Remove Media Controls** uninstalls it.
- **Sleep timer.** `/da sleep 30` pauses after 30 minutes with a gentle fade; `/da stopafter` stops when the current song ends.
- **New shortcuts** (unbound until you assign them): show/hide HUD, show/hide lyrics HUD, favorite current song, shuffle, repeat.
- **Search in Settings.** Type in the box above the settings to find any option across all sections.
- **Auto-updating lists.** History adds **Recently Added** and **Never Played**.

## HUD

- **Hide When Idle:** hides the HUD after music has been paused or stopped for a time you choose (1 second to 2 minutes), by sliding it away or fading it out slowly. The lyrics HUD fades with it.
- **Song Change Card:** briefly shows the new song's title, artist and artwork when the song changes, with a slide or fade animation. Move and resize it in Edit HUD Layout.
- **Song Change Animation:** the new title, artist and artwork fade in.
- **Classic HUD:** optional "Next:" line, and the song's time under the progress bar or on the artist line.
- HUD settings are grouped into Appearance, Visibility and Motion, Song Change Card and Progress Bar.

## Improvements

- **Beveled finish** is now clearly visible on wave, spike and Rounded Bars spectrum styles.
- **Player progress bar** matches the HUD's: same rail, colors and finish.
- **PiP** keeps only one dependency package; older packages and interrupted downloads are removed whenever PiP setup runs.
- Setting rows align their checkboxes, arrows and values in one column.

## Compatibility

Existing libraries, playlists, lyrics, Up Next and settings remain compatible. Install **`darkmusic-3.5.0.jar`** with **Minecraft 26.2**, **Java 25**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.5+** and **Fabric API for 26.2**. PiP and Media Controls stay optional and install through their menus; each version pins its own packages, so existing PiP users are asked to install the matching v3.5.0 package. **Do not put the dependency ZIPs in `mods`**. PiP and Media Controls require Windows x64; the music player supports Windows, Linux and macOS.

releases.notes:
# DarkMusic v3.4.0

## Chat commands

Control playback from chat. Every command works as `/da …` or `/darkmusic …`.

- **`/da play [song]`** resumes playback, or plays a song by name. Press Tab while typing to see matching titles from your library.
- **`/da pause`**, **`/da stop`**, **`/da previous`** and **`/da next`** control the player.
- **`/da now`** shows the current song, position, volume and speed, with clickable Previous, Play, Pause, Next, Stop and Lyrics buttons.
- **`/da queue <song>`** adds a song to Up Next.
- **`/da volume [0–100]`**, **`/da mute`** and **`/da speed [0.5–3]`** show or set the value.
- **`/da seek <time>`** jumps to a time such as `1:30` or `90`, or moves by `+10` or `-10` seconds.
- **`/da shuffle [on|off]`** and **`/da repeat [off|one|all]`** work like the player's buttons and are saved.
- **`/da keys`** lists your current DarkMusic shortcuts, with a **Change Keys** button that opens Key Binds.

## A new `/da help`

`/da help` now fits in open chat and uses your menu accent color. Commands are grouped into Playback, Screens and More. Click a command to put it in the chat box, or hover over it for details. Links to the user guide, releases and issue reporting are buttons at the bottom.

## Fixes

- **`/da update` asks first.** It used to start downloading as soon as it found an update. It now shows the new version with **Download and Install** and **Release Notes** buttons, and nothing downloads until you click.
- **No confirmation dialog for DarkMusic buttons.** Clicking a DarkMusic button in chat no longer opens Minecraft's "run this command?" dialog. Installing an update still needs the command typed or DarkMusic's own button, so a link sent by a server cannot start a download.
- **Screens open from chat.** Buttons in chat that open a screen, such as **Change Keys** and **Lyrics**, now replace the chat box instead of doing nothing.

## Compatibility

Existing libraries, playlists, lyrics, Up Next and settings remain compatible. Install **`darkmusic-3.4.0.jar`** with **Minecraft 26.2**, **Java 25**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.5+** and **Fabric API for 26.2**. PiP stays optional and installs through its menu. Each version pins its own PiP package, so existing PiP users are asked to install the matching v3.4.0 package there; settings and permissions are kept. **Do not put the dependency ZIP in `mods`**. Native PiP requires Windows x64; the music player supports Windows, Linux and macOS.


PiP native package (helper and runtime) SHA-256: `475042f63c401b3152a93f6fad644c5dcd5845ac5000ba3b62a0a04699f7503c`

# DarkMusic v3.3.4

## Spectrum

- **Beveled waves and spikes.** With the Beveled spectrum finish, Smooth Wave, Filled Wave, Spike and Filled Spike now look clearly shaded instead of almost flat. Light follows the curve: rising edges catch the light and falling edges fall into shadow, matching the upper-left light on Bars. Filled Wave and Filled Spike also fade from bright near the edge to shaded at the base.
- **Beveled Rounded Bars.** Rounded Bars now get the same lit left side, shaded right side and slightly darker face as Bars, instead of shading only their rounded ends.

Bars, the Circular HUD and the Flat finish look the same as before.

## Compatibility

Existing libraries, playlists, lyrics, Up Next and settings remain compatible. Install **`darkmusic-3.3.4.jar`** with **Minecraft 26.2**, **Java 25**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.5+** and **Fabric API for 26.2**. PiP stays optional and installs through its menu. releases.notes:
# DarkMusic v3.3.3

## Fixes

- **Lyrics after Reset to Defaults.** After a reset, newly downloaded songs once again look up their lyrics automatically, and caption lookups no longer use the download service that the reset closed.
- **Settings load with an unusual `options.txt`.** If Minecraft's `options.txt` is not valid UTF-8, DarkMusic warns and still loads your settings instead of failing.
- **Download reviews are no longer lost.** If a second batch with songs already in your library is queued while an earlier "already in library" review is still open, the newer review now replaces it. Before, the newer one was silently dropped.
- **Safer self-update.** If the update cannot move the old mod JAR aside, the installer withdraws the new JAR, so the `mods` folder never ends up with both versions or with neither. When both versions have the same file name, a failed swap now restores the original even if the backup cannot be moved back.
- **No clicks when changing tempo at low sample rates.** Pitch-preserving tempo no longer clicks or skips on audio at 22.05 kHz and below.
- **Download range errors stay on the form.** Range and All are checked before queuing, so an invalid range is reported beside the fields.
- **Spectrum HUD at very high detail.** When the spectrum needs more geometry than expected, the extra detail is skipped instead of interrupting HUD rendering.
- Smaller fixes: a library rescan that empties the library cannot throw while the HUD or shortcuts show the first song, PiP setup always releases its runtime when closed during setup, and Circular HUD waveform bar gaps are measured at the base of the bars.

## Under the hood

- One shared SHA-256 helper replaces ten copies.
- Faster duplicate-cache saves when migrating a large legacy cache, and the song list no longer compares itself against rows it has not built yet.

## Compatibility

Existing libraries, playlists, lyrics, Up Next and settings remain compatible. Install **`darkmusic-3.3.3.jar`** with **Minecraft 26.2**, **Java 25**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.5+** and **Fabric API for 26.2**. PiP stays optional and installs through its menu. Each version pins its own PiP package, so existing PiP users are asked to install the matching v3.3.3 package there; settings and permissions are kept. **Do not put the dependency ZIP in `mods`**. Native PiP requires Windows x64; the music player supports Windows, Linux and macOS.
